items.t: '엔비디아칩 독주 저지'…MS "자체 AI칩 내년 백만개 이상 투입"
items.fullText: 핫픽! 미국주식 핫픽! 미국주식 '엔비디아칩 독주 저지'…MS "자체 AI칩 내년 백만개 이상 투입" 입력 2026.10.13 00:01 수정 2026.10.13 00:17 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 김정아 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. MS "업계 최고 수준의 전력 효율과 메모리 대역폭" 공언 "자체 클라우드 시스템을 위한 주요 AI 추론 시스템으로 활용" 사티아 나델라 마이크로소프트 최고경영자(CEO·왼쪽)와 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO가 7일(현지시간) 미국 샌프란시스코에서 양사가 공동개발한 인공지능(AI)용 노트북 RTX 스파크 울트라 시리즈 앞에서 대화하고 있다. AFP연합뉴스 마이크로소프트는 자체 설계한 차세대 맞춤형 AI칩을 내부 AI서비스 지원용으로 내년에 백만 개 이상 배치할 계획이라고 발표했다. 이 칩은 업계 최고 수준의 메모리 대역폭을 갖고 있다고 회사는 강조했다. 12일(현지시간) 블룸버그 등 외신들에 따르면, 마이크로소프트는 이 날 자체 설계한 차세대 맞춤형 칩 마이아 300을 공개했다. 이 칩은 마이크로소프트가 자체 개발한 AI 데이터 처리 칩의 3세대 제품으로, 코딩이나 복잡한 비즈니스 작업을 사용자 대신 수행하는 데 최적화돼있다. 이전 세대 제품은 이미 마이크로소프트의 자체 AI 모델과 마이크로소프트의 애져 클라우드 컴퓨팅 서비스에서 제공되는 오픈AI의 모델을 구동하는 데 사용되고 있다. 회사는 블로그 게시물에서 마이아가 "마이크로소프트 제품 및 서비스를 위한 주요 AI 추론 시스템이 될 것"이라고 밝혔다. 또 내년부터 마이아 300 칩을 수 기가와트 규모로 대량 생산할 계획이라고 언급했다. 마이크로소프트는 마이아 300 실리콘에 탑재된 중앙 컴퓨팅 프로세서는 핵심 컴퓨팅 기능은 대만 TSMC의 2나노 기술로 제작된 칩렛으로 구성되고 프로세서에서 시스템 내부 다른 곳으로 데이터를 이동하는 기능 등에는 3나노 기술을 사용한다고 설명했다. 또 업계 최고 수준의 메모리 대역폭을 갖고 있다고 밝혔다. 마이크로소프트는 마이아 300 프로세서는 96개의 칩이 들어가는 랙에 탑재되며 약 167킬로와트의 전력을 소비한다고 언급했다. 이는 엔비디아의 최신 GB300 AI 서버 랙(그래픽 처리 장치(GPU) 72개 탑재)이 사용하는 142킬로와트와 비교된다. 회사는 마이아 300 칩이 "주요 GPU 기반 시스템"보다 메가와트당 약 40% 더 많은 토큰을 생성할 수 있다"고 주장했다. 마이크로소프트의 애져 하드웨어 시스템 및 인프라 부문 사장인 라니 보르카르는 “기본적으로 시스템 전체를 최적화해 모든 와트, 모든 달러, 모든 바이트의 메모리에서 더 많은 지능을 제공한다”고 말했다. 최근 알파벳의 구글과 아마존 같은 클라우드 컴퓨팅 경쟁업체와 오픈AI 등 AI연구소들은 엔비디아 칩에 대한 의존도를 낮추기 위해 맞춤형 칩을 잇따라 출시하고 있다. 마이크로소프트는 구글과 아마존보다 자체 칩 개발이 늦어졌다. 마이크로소프트의 자체 칩 확대가 엔비디아 GPU의 구매를 대체하는지, 아니면 전체 AI 컴퓨팅 용량을 추가로 확대하는 것인지는 알려지지 않았다. 또 AI 기능 작동에 필수적인 기억과 추론 기능을 위해 어떤 메모리를 사용하는지도 확인되지 않았다. 그러나 상당량의 AI추론을 대규모로 처리하기 위해서는 상당한 메모리 용량과 대역폭이 필요할 것으로 보인다. 마이크로소프트는 올해 자본 지출에 1,750억 달러 이상을 투자할 것이라고 발표했다. 김정아 객원기자 kja@hankyung.com 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니

items.fullText: OCP Global Summit: Amid Ecosystem Adoption, NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Help Scale AI Factories Worldwide Cisco, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Visionbay are joining many making advances with Vera Rubin. October 12, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! As AI factories grow from megawatts to gigawatts, building them takes more than advanced computing. Open standards are helping the industry scale AI infrastructure faster, more efficiently and more reliably. At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place in the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, NVIDIA announced new partnerships and contributions aimed at creating a common foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure. NVIDIA contributed key NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack and compute tray designs to OCP through the open NVIDIA MGX architecture, giving system builders a common foundation for developing next-generation AI factory infrastructure. Together, these efforts span the AI factory itself, the utility grid that powers it and the rack-scale architecture at the heart of modern accelerated computing. NVIDIA and Partners Announce Open Architecture Advances At the OCP event, NVIDIA and partners made a handful of announcements: NVIDIA and hyperscalers published open standards for next-generation AI factories, including AI factory design standards and grid resilience. NVIDIA launched new open source software components for NVIDIA DSX AI Factory. Meta and NVIDIA advanced open AI networking with NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet SuperNIC and Spectrum-6 innovations. Visionbay introduced an 800V DC AI factory design for the Vera Rubin era. NVIDIA and Cisco announced the Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP) standard, the industry’s first module ​for 400Gb/s-based networking fabrics. items.fullText: AI·SW SW 래블업, '한국어 AI 추론 속도 향상' 드래프트 모델 공개 발행일 : 2026-10-12 18:16 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 래블업이 GLM-5.2 오픈소스를 공개한 허깅페이스 모델저장소 캡쳐 화면. 래블업 래블업은 한국어 기반 거대언어모델(LLM)의 답변 속도를 높이는 드래프트 모델 'GLM-5.2-NVFP4-DFlash-ko'를 오픈소스로 공개했다고 12일 밝혔다. 이번 모델은 한글날인 9일 공개됐다. 한국어 질의와 한국어 기반 에이전트 작업에서 LLM 추론을 가속화하는 드래프트 모델이다. 중국 즈푸(Z.ai)의 'GLM-5.2'를 엔비디아 4비트 부동소수점 형식(NVFP4)으로 구동할 때 함께 활용한다. 지랩(z-lab)이 공개한 디플래시(DFlash) 방식을 적용했다. 디플래시는 토큰 여러 개를 동시에 생성하는 방식이다. 드래프트 모델이 여러 토큰을 미리 예측하면 대형 모델이 이를 한 번에 검증해 답변 품질을 유지하면서 생성 속도를 높인다. 래블업은 영어 기반 드래프트 모델이 한국어 작업에서 가속 효과가 떨어지는 문제를 개선했다. 한국어 데이터로 모델을 학습해 추측 적중률을 높였다. 한국어 에이전트 트래픽에서 측정한 평균 수락 길이(MAL)는 한국어 질의 2.77로 영어 모델과 유사한 가속 성능을 기록했다. 래블업은 한국어 디퓨전 언어 모델도 개발 중이다. 약 110억 파라미터(매개변수) 규모로, 로컬 기기에서 에이전트 작업을 수행하는 온디바이스 모델 개발이 목표다. 학습은 B200 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 64장 규모 클러스터를 활용한다. 신정규 래블업 대표는 “개발자와 기업이 한국어 환경에서도 가속 효과를 얻을 수 있도록 한글날에 맞춰 한국어 드래프트 모델을 공개했다”며 “AI 인프라 소프트웨어(SW)를 개발한 경험을 바탕으로 한국어 모델 개발까지 사업 영역을 확대하고 있다”고 말했다. 래블업은 최근 금융위원회에 증권신고서를 제출하고 코스닥 상장 절차에 착수했다. 공모 주식수는 총 218만주로, 희망 공모가는 2만원에서 2만3000원이다. 래블업은 오는 13일부터 19일까지 기관투자자 대상 수요예측을 진행할 예정이다. 조벼리 기자 starry@etnews.com

items.fullText: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents See how developers are combining AI agents with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, test physical behavior and guide improvements. October 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Build a Humanoid Simulator for a Warehouse Environment 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Humanoid-Warehouse.mp4 Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view. Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views. DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics ( ovphysx ), scene updates ( ovstage ), rendering ( ovrtx ) and the user interface ( ovui ). items.fullText: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents RTX Spark Preorders open today alongside a preview of NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows, the first deskside AI supercomputer built for the Windows enterprise desktop. October 7, 2026 by Gerardo Delgado 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At a Microsoft event in San Francisco on Wednesday, Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella outlined how NVIDIA and Microsoft are co-engineering hardware and software for AI agents to run on Windows PCs. NVIDIA was founded because of Windows, Huang said. Now AI agents are coming to Windows. “If you look at the entire journey of our company, Windows was at the core of it,” Huang said, tracing back NVIDIA’s support for Windows and Microsoft over several decades. “If not for Windows there would be no GeForce.” NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang connected that history — and his long-term vision — to the agentic era Wednesday during a fireside chat with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella hosted by Sriram Krishnan, a former senior White House policy advisor on AI at the Windows AI and Surface event, held at Dogpatch Studios in San Francisco. “The thing that I really give Jensen all the credit for, quite frankly, is that consistency of vision of what this can be—not today, not tomorrow, but as a secular trend,” Nadella said. “And that’s what brings us to this moment.” “The personal computer is the ultimate tool, it’s my ultimate tool, and for a whole generation of people, it’s our ultimate tool,” Huang said. “What happens in the era of agents, when the agent is on your computer? items.fullText: Why Telecom Operators Are Building Their AI Strategy on Open Models Telcos are turning to open models to build trusted, production‑ready AI workflows they can deploy, customize and govern across their most critical workloads. October 6, 2026 by Kanika Atri 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Telecom operators are increasingly building their AI strategies on open models — and the reasons go beyond mere cost. Open models give telcos the ability to trust, control and customize AI across their most critical workloads — from autonomous networks to customer care. NVIDIA’s latest State of AI in Telecommunications report reflects this shift, with 89% of respondents reporting that open source models and software are important to their company’s AI strategy. For operators, the strategic value of open models is fivefold: They expand access to frontier‑level intelligence at lower cost, allowing operators to reserve closed models for the workloads where they drive the most value. Independent benchmarks such as the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 show that leading open models are becoming more competitive across demanding reasoning, coding, scientific and agentic workloads. They support telco‑specific customization, with open weights and training recipes that operators can fine‑tune for their own operations using network, customer and industry data. They enable trustworthy AI by giving telcos greater visibility into and control over model artifacts and behavior, so models can be evaluated, adapted and governed in alignment with regulations and business policies. They enable flexible, secure deployment: teams can size and optimize open models to run across public clouds, private infrastructure and edge environments. They unlock the opportunity for telcos to deliver locally adapted AI services to enterprise and government customers by hosting and fine-tuning open models. items.fullText: Productive, Durable, Fungible: How NVIDIA AI Factories Maximize Return on Investment AI factories generating the strongest returns are the ones built to earn more, last longer and serve more kinds of work. October 1, 2026 by Shruti Koparkar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI factories are built by the megawatt, even by the gigawatt. Each megawatt factory costs roughly $60 million, and AI factory operators will only commit capital on that scale with a clear view of the return on investment. Three key things shape AI factory returns: Earning capacity: What the factory could earn in a year if it sold every token it can produce. Useful life : How long its AI hardware keeps earning. Demand : How much demand there is for those tokens. Strength cannot fully offset weakness in another. High earning capacity counts for little if the factory sells only part of what it can produce. High demand matters little if it stops producing at full capacity in just a year. Nor are the three independent. A factory that can run more kinds of workloads finds more demand, keeping it earning year after year. NVIDIA AI factories are engineered to maximize all three. They’re: Productive : Delivering the highest throughput per megawatt and the lowest cost per token, which maximizes their earning capacity . Durable : NVIDIA GPUs and systems keep earning years after they ship, extending useful life . Fungible : They run every type of AI — in every phase and every place — as well as many workloads that don’t involve AI at all, which deepens and broadens the demand they can serve. NVIDIA platform is productive, durable and fungible, which maximizes AI factory returns. Engineering codesign across the full stack maximizes AI factory throughput, and continuous software optimization keeps installed hardware productive years after it ships. items.fullText: NVIDIA Opens Applications for 2027–2028 Graduate Fellowships With Awards Up to $60,000 September 30, 2026 by Sharon Gibbons 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Bringing together the world’s brightest minds and the latest accelerated computing technology leads to powerful breakthroughs that help tackle some of the biggest research problems. To foster such innovation, the NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program provides grants, mentors and technical support to doctoral students doing outstanding research relevant to NVIDIA technologies. The program, in its 26th year, is now accepting applications worldwide. It focuses on supporting students working in AI, machine learning, autonomous vehicles, computer graphics, robotics, healthcare, high-performance computing and related fields. Awards are up to $60,000 per student. Since its start in 2002, the Graduate Fellowship Program has awarded over 220 grants worth around $8 million. Students must have completed at least their first year of Ph.D.-level studies at the time of application. The application deadline for the 2027-2028 academic year is October 30, 2026. An in-person internship at an NVIDIA research office preceding the fellowship year is mandatory; eligible candidates must be available for the internship in summer 2027. For more on eligibility and how to apply, visit the program website . Featured image shows last year’s NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship recipients. items.fullText: How Open Science Can Help Researchers Prepare for the Next Pandemic NVIDIA is collaborating with organizations including Google DeepMind and the European Molecular Biology Laboratory’s European Bioinformatics Institute to release an open dataset of viral protein structures — giving scientists a head start against diseases. September 24, 2026 by Anthony Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! When COVID-19 emerged, scientists had a crucial advantage: Decades of prior research on coronaviruses meant they understood the virus’ key proteins well enough to design vaccines in record time. The next pandemic may not offer the same head start. To help improve the odds, NVIDIA has joined a coalition of global research organizations, including Google DeepMind and the European Molecular Biology Laboratory’s European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI), to release predicted 3D structures for the protein complexes of more than 2,800 viruses — openly available to any scientist, anywhere, through the AlphaFold Database. The structures in the newly released dataset were inferred using AlphaFold2 — Google DeepMind’s AI model for predicting how proteins fold into 3D shapes — with optimization from NVIDIA BioNeMo Inference Runtime . This allowed the team to scale inference to thousands of viral proteomes, predicting the complexes, or groups of interacting proteins, encoded within each virus. “Our ambition with the AlphaFold Database has always been to democratize access to foundational biology at scale,” said Risha Patel, life sciences partnerships manager at Google DeepMind. “This collaboration to bring thousands of viral complexes into the database will equip scientists around the world with insights they need to help prepare for future outbreaks.” NVIDIA is also openly releasing the BioNeMo Structure Prediction Pipeline , the GPU-accelerated workflow used to generate the dataset, so researchers can go from protein sequence to predicted 3D

items.fullText: Sakeena Fiza Helps NVIDIA Hardware Succeed at Scale By testing systems from lab bring-up to production, validation engineers turn cutting-edge hardware into dependable infrastructure. September 23, 2026 by Matthew Leib 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! When Sakeena Fiza describes her work as a validation engineer at NVIDIA, she does so in terms more befitting a detective story than a world-class engineering lab. “Validation engineers look in the shadows and shine a light into every corner,” Fiza said. “Every time we get a system, our first thought is: how can it break?” And when it does? “I always like to think of it as a mystery to solve,” she said. At NVIDIA, the systems Fiza and her colleagues in the data center systems engineering lab investigate are the engines of the AI era. Her work begins before the rest of the world knows a product exists — in the lab — when a new system first receives power. Components are brought up one by one, boards are integrated, firmware and software teams swarm, and engineers watch for the first signs of life. One of Fiza’s earliest and most enduring memories of working at NVIDIA is the collective joy she experienced when she saw the NVIDIA Rubin GPU working for the first time at a system level. “It literally just said, ‘NVIDIA Corporation Device,’” she recalls. “And everyone’s cheering and celebrating because it’s the first time in the world that a Rubin GPU enumerated at a system level.” Those moments, electric as they are, are only the beginning. From there, the system must be made resilient: from tray to rack to cluster to production line to customer AI factory. The ROS open framework is a project from Open Robotics that helps humans build robots. NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 — a collection of GPU-accelerated packages built on ROS, released today at the ROSCon conference in Toronto, Canada — helps humans and AI agents build robots together. ROS provides the open source foundation for much of modern robotics development, giving developers common tools, libraries and standards for building and connecting robot applications. NVIDIA Isaac ROS brings NVIDIA accelerated computing, physical AI models and production-ready libraries to the nearly 1.3 million ROS users, helping developers build high-performance robotics applications using free, familiar, open source tools. Choosing products that fit the complete factory design helps builders turn computing capacity into useful AI output. To help builders make those decisions, NVIDIA is introducing NVIDIA DSX Ready, a qualification program for partner products and solutions that meet applicable NVIDIA DSX AI factory reference design requirements. The program launches with two initial categories: battery energy storage systems (BESS) and cooling distribution units (CDUs). Category-specific requirements and review through the program help builders evaluate offerings with greater confidence, reduce integration risk and move toward deployment. That system view matters now because optimizing one part of an AI factory can shift the bottleneck elsewhere.
